subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` physically remove stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files under the existing retention rules and report those removals in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and evidence-backed, but accepting physical session-archive removal intersects open session retention and data-durability policy that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
options.body: Land the PR if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and the provided CLI proof.

options.title: Require broader upgrade proof
options.body: Ask for a larger real-store or upgrade-style cleanup transcript before merge if retained artifacts are still a concern.

options.title: Defer to archive policy work
options.body: Pause or close the PR if maintainers want the no-delete/archive naming policy settled before changing cleanup behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the PR if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and the provided CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the relevant sessions cleanup UX and maintenance controls that this PR changes at the operator boundary.
